framework.name: NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework

outcomes: Authority, evidence, review, and release claims are separated.
Security gaps retain named ownership and cannot be silently converted to completion.
Source-contract evidence is labeled separately from behavioral evidence.
Model, policy, tool, browser, terminal, web, extension, and inter-agent trust boundaries are explicit.
Untrusted provenance and external effects are represented in machine-readable contracts.
Third-party and extension identities are mapped to exact capabilities and trust domains.
Supported models are evaluated by protocol, coding, browser, research, and safety suites.
Secrets, dependencies, performance, leaks, false completion, unauthorized effects, and recovery are measurable.
Measurement outputs have deterministic digests and benchmark dashboards can be signed.
Privileged effects are fail-closed behind the authority service and scoped grants.
Unknown external effects enter reconciliation and are not blindly retried.
Convergence, cancellation, revocation, compensation, and recovery have explicit state transitions.

riskRegister.risk: P1A production Owner Mode lacks completed tri-platform behavioral evidence and independent review.
riskRegister.closure: Signed platform receipts, independent review, owner approval, protected-main activation.

riskRegister.risk: Long-duration resource leaks or authority drift may only emerge during sustained execution.
riskRegister.closure: A real 24-hour sample corpus passes the P8 soak gate.

riskRegister.risk: Full-host execution, browser, IPC, updater, MCP/A2A, signing, and prompt-injection paths require independent adversarial review.
riskRegister.closure: Independent penetration-test receipt has no unresolved critical/high finding.

riskRegister.risk: Human operators may over-trust autonomous actions or fail to understand takeover/recovery states.
riskRegister.closure: P5-015 independent human usability review is complete.
